_meta.purpose: The durable list of OPEN leads. A lead recorded only in a chat transcript is lost at the next compaction, and a lead recorded only in gen_prompts.py cannot be checked -- nothing in the fleet reports which queue item a job took, so a lead that was tried and failed looks identical to one nobody ever attempted. Each entry below carries a WITNESS: a grep against the live seed tree that matches WHILE THE LEAD IS STILL OPEN. Run check_leads.py to turn 'do we remember this?' into 'is it still in the tree?'.
_meta.usage:
python3 check_leads.py            # status of every lead
python3 check_leads.py --open     # only the ones still open
_meta.status_values: open = witness still matches, nobody has landed it. landed = witness gone, RE-PRICE THE SIBLINGS. unverifiable = no mechanical witness exists; must be checked by hand.
_meta.rule: When a lead flips to landed, do not just delete it -- the pattern that paid once is a reason to CHECK the next instance, never a reason to assume it. Re-derive the siblings against the new tree before requeueing them.
_meta.trees: THREE tree locations, NOT interchangeable. records/<slug>/ is the LEADER's tree, reseeded from whoever holds the record -- this is what jobs are seeded from and therefore what a lead must beat. projs/<slug>/Solution/ is OUR working tree; it equals records/ only on slugs where we lead (on keccak-f1600 ours is theta 3200 against the record's 2240, so reading the wrong one INVERTS the answer). out/<slug>/ is per-job scratch, wiped and re-extracted for the very next job -- a constant read there belongs to whichever job landed last. check_leads.py resolves records/ then projs/ then out/, in that order.
_meta.price_zero: price 0 means UNPRICED, not worthless -- a lead whose mechanism is confirmed but whose row count has not been derived. Derive it before queueing, and write the number back here. Only fb-queue-stale is genuinely a 0 (it is queue hygiene).
_meta.fixed_challenge_rule: THE FIXED-CHALLENGE VACUITY RULE. Our soundness obligation is a Lean theorem `soundness : forall env, constraints_hold env -> spec env` -- unconditional, over ALL witnesses, with no random oracle and no computational assumption. So EVERY published protocol that gets its efficiency from a verifier challenge is unavailable to us in its published form, and the failure is not subtle. Worked out on Wesolowski's proof of exponentiation, whose check is pi^l * g^r = y with l the challenge and r = 2^t mod l public: with l fixed at compile time the prover picks ANY pi and outputs y := pi^l * g^r, which verifies by construction at zero work. Because gcd(l, |G|) = 1 makes pi |-> pi^l g^r a BIJECTION of G, every y has an accepting proof -- the equation is a DEFINITION of y, not a constraint on it, and the gadget proves nothing. Wesolowski's own soundness reduction is to the adaptive root game (output u, THEN receive l, THEN produce v with v^l = u); fixing l reverses the quantifiers and the game is won by sampling v and setting u := v^l. Pietrzak has the identical disease with fixed round challenges, and his footnote 5 records an attack that works merely from omitting y from the hash. GENERALISATION, AND THIS IS THE TEST TO APPLY: given a proposed 'witness the answer, check a relation at a fixed public point' construction, ask whether the check is SURJECTIVE onto the claimed output as the free witness ranges over its domain. If it is, the construction is vacuous. THE ESCAPE, WHEN IT EXISTS: if the relation is a polynomial identity of degree d in the challenge, checking it at d+1 DISTINCT FIXED points forces the identity itself and no challenge is needed -- this is derandomisation, not Fiat-Shamir, and it is sound unconditionally. That is the only route by which any challenge-based protocol enters this cost model. See the ecip-derandomized lead.

leads.summary: UNBLOCKED AND WIDENED. The top majority bit of EVERY Sigma AND sigma word is free, not just sigma: in the carry-save form each enters with coefficient -2, so bit 31 contributes -2*2^31*maj31 = -2^32*maj31 == 0 mod 2^32. 224 gadget bits per block at <1,1> = 448 score.
leads.note:
THE BLOCKER THIS ENTRY RAISED IS NOW ANSWERED, so it can be executed. It said 'check the fused-reduction carry widths FIRST -- the addend becomes [0,2^33) and if any carry sits on a power-of-two boundary the saving is cancelled.' MEASURED over 4.2e5 states including saturated extremes: under the fused round the quotient is e' in {0..6} (3 bits) and a' in {0..8} (4 bits). Neither sits on a boundary, so the saving stands. Independently re-derived and machine-verified on 2e5 random inputs for all four functions.
WIDENED: the original entry covered only the two sigma functions. The criterion is v2(coefficient) + j >= 32, and in the carry-save form Sigma0/Sigma1 also enter at coefficient -2, so their bit 31 is free too. Maj and Ch enter at coefficient +1 and have NO free bit -- do not try to extend it to them. Per block: 64 rounds x 2 Sigmas + 48 schedule steps x 2 sigmas = 224 gadget bits.
FIRST STEP: change the Sigma/sigma loop bound from j < 32 to j < 31, define N = sum_{j<31} 2^j maj_j, and re-derive the consumer's quotient width against the numbers above.
DEPENDS ON the carry-save rewrite (sha-carrysave) being in place -- the free bit only exists once the word is expressed as [rot+rot+rot] - 2N. Do that one first.

leads.summary: CLOSED -- theta is already at the floor of its gadget family. Three independent lines of evidence agree. Do NOT requeue without new mathematics.
leads.note:
CLOSED 2026-08-10 on converging evidence from three independent methods:
(1) THE SLP SEARCH WAS ACTUALLY RUN (tools/theta_slp.py). Boyar-Peralta generalised to 3-input XOR gates over the free module GF(2)^25 (+) GF(2)^25 with rot1 as a shift operator, randomised restarts. Best found h = 35 lane-gates, VERIFIED against a reference Keccak theta. Naive baseline 40. The record is ALSO 35 (records/keccak-f1600/Cost.lean: ThetaC 640 + ThetaXor 1600 = 2240 alloc/round = 35 x 64). The search reproduced the record's own construction and found nothing better -- the winning method it reports is 'absorbed-D', which IS the record's theta-D fusion.
(2) cvc5 QF_FF exact synthesis over BN254 proves parity-5 is UNSAT at one row AND unsat at two rows with one witness (multipliers allowed to vanish). So the 5-way column parity cannot beat two XOR3 in this gadget family -- not a heuristic failure, a proof.
(3) A proposal to drop C and build D directly as a parity-of-10 by free-sum bit extraction (7 score/bit) was arithmetically checked and is 960/round WORSE, not better -- the claim of a 23,040 win had the sign backwards. THE REASON IS THE POINT: the record's output gate is XOR3(A, C[x-1], rot1 C[x+1]), which absorbs BOTH column parities, so D is never materialised and already costs exactly zero. Materialising D can only lose, however cheaply you build it. Record 4480/round vs proposal 5440/round.
WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: only a gadget family outside 'one row, one non-vanishing affine multiplier' -- e.g. a 3-row/2-witness gadget emitting TWO C bits jointly. cvc5 can decide that; the generator is reusable. Until then keccak's remaining value is entirely in kec-port-record (122880), not here.
*** THE PROCESS LESSON: this lead was priced at 15360 off a formula, 'score = 153600 + 48h, record h = 640, floor h = 320', that nobody had checked against the tree. h in that formula was ThetaC's per-round ALLOCATIONS (640), while the SLP search's h counts LANE-GATES (35). Two different units, and the 'proved floor of 320' was half of a number that was already optimal. A price derived from a formula is not a price until the units are pinned to a Cost.lean line. ***

*** UPGRADED FROM 'SEARCH FOUND NOTHING' TO A STRUCTURAL OBSTRUCTION, and this is the part worth keeping. ***
The bit-level model was rebuilt from scratch and reproduces the record construction and 184320 EXACTLY, verified against a reference Keccak theta at both bit and 64-bit-word level. So the model is trustworthy and the record is tied, not beaten.
THE COORDINATE SYSTEM: the 320 column-slices form a SINGLE 320-CYCLE under (x,b) -> (x+2, b-1). Each slice-seed is an edge, and the rider of edge n lives in node n+128. Only 320 seeds need construction; the other 1280 targets are free siblings. Anyone attacking this again should start there rather than from the lane picture.
WHY 639 RESISTS, three obstructions, in increasing order of force:
(1) Every count is exactly saturated -- a node has 5 atoms = exactly two fanin-3 gates (3, then +2), and a target has weight 11 = exactly rider + P + P = 3 slots. There is no slack anywhere to absorb a saved gate.
(2) Every shortcut is circular: C[x][b] = T xor rider xor C[x+2][b-1] is one helper, but that target itself needs C[x][b]. Every relation of this shape closes on itself.
(3) THE DECISIVE ONE, AND IT IS A MODULAR INVARIANT, NOT A SEARCH RESULT. The 3-column 9->8 repair that motivated this whole lead WAS reproduced and verified -- and then decoded: node 2's parity costs only one helper because two of its five atoms arrive free as riders of already-built targets, one cancelled by a neighbour's dirty wire. That mechanism requires the rider offset k on the node cycle to be <= 2. MEASURED: 3-column w=1 has k = 2, so it works. EVERY 5-column instance has k == 3 (mod 5): w=1 -> 3, w=2 -> 8, w=4 -> 8, w=64 -> 128. Since 3 is not 0, 1 or 2 mod 5, THE COINCIDENCE CANNOT OCCUR FOR KECCAK THETA AT ANY LANE WIDTH.
MATCHING NEGATIVE SEARCHES (seeded from the record, delete one helper, anneal to repair, helpers allowed to consume produced targets): 5-node cycle 10->9 failed over 367 restarts; 10-node 20->19 failed; 20-node 40->39 failed -- each stuck at exactly 10 unresolved targets, the two slices flanking the crippled node. The 3-node cycle repaired in 49 restarts. So the 3-column result is a genuine FALSE FRIEND: it is real, it is verified, and it does not generalise.
WHAT IS LEFT, IF ANYTHING: the search held lanes uniform, which is a self-imposed constraint the real bit-level problem does not require. Any win must be a NON-UNIFORM bit-level scheme that breaks the k == 3 (mod 5) invariant or routes around it. The corpus's h >= 320 floor claim is untouched by this work and the 320-to-640 gap is real, but no mechanism crossing it was found.
MY OWN BRIEF WAS WRONG ON THE UNITS AND THE AGENT HAD TO RECONCILE IT: I wrote 'standing record is h = 640, even h = 639 is a record'. Under the literal lane-level rules the textbook schedule is 40 gates, so 'beat 640' would be trivial. The challenge is BIT-level: score = 153600 + 48h with h counting HELPER gates only, the 1600 target Xor3 rows already sitting inside the 153600 base, and the record h = 640 = 320 column-slices x 2 helpers. Writing a brief in the wrong units nearly wasted the whole run.
ARTIFACTS: tools/theta_slp.py (lane SLP + searches), tools/theta_bits.py (bit-level model + record verification), tools/theta_repair.py (the decisive repair search), tools/theta_anneal.py, tools/theta_slp_result.json, tools/repair_3_1.json.
THE FOUR ANALOGUES, WITH THEIR EVIDENCE STRENGTH STATED HONESTLY (cols/w -> node cycle, rider offset k, h-1 repair result): 3/1 -> 3, k=2, REPAIRED in 49 restarts. 5/1 -> 5, k=3, failed over 367 restarts. 5/2 -> 10, k=8, failed over 62 restarts. 5/4 -> 20, k=8, failed -- BUT THIS LAST ROW IS THE WEAKEST POINT: the run was killed once the pattern was established, and its label comes from an earlier 60-second pass that recorded the deletion as unrepaired after only 16 deletions tried. Treat 5/4 as suggestive, not established. The invariant argument, not the search, is what closes this lead.

leads.summary: ECIP: verify Q = kP by a divisor witness + Weil reciprocity instead of an addition chain. ~89 F_p multiplications, and witness degrees are INDEPENDENT of scalar bit-length (measured: identical degrees at 8/32/64/128/200/255 bits). The open question is whether it can be DERANDOMIZED.
leads.source: secp256k1 alternative-formulations research, 2026-08-10, verified empirically against garaga on secp256k1
leads.note:
*** SOUNDNESS CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH RESULT, AND IT IS THE WHOLE LEAD. *** The agent proposed deriving the challenge point A0 by hashing the witness with an in-circuit Poseidon, and argued the premise 'no Fiat-Shamir available' was wrong because grinding costs ~2^250. THAT ARGUMENT DOES NOT APPLY HERE. Our obligation is a Lean theorem `soundness : forall env, constraints_hold env -> spec env` -- UNCONDITIONAL, over ALL witnesses, with no random oracle and no computational assumption. 'The adversary would need 2^250 hash evaluations' is not a proof of that statement and cannot be made into one. A fixed public A0 is worse, not better: the prover chooses the divisor witness knowing A0. So ECIP AS PUBLISHED IS NOT DIRECTLY EXPRESSIBLE. WHAT MIGHT SAVE IT, AND THIS IS THE ACTUAL LEAD: the witness degrees are TINY -- measured n+1/n+2/n+2/n+5, i.e. 2/3/3/6 at n=1. A polynomial identity of degree d is forced by checking it at d+1 distinct FIXED points. So check the Weil-reciprocity identity at ~7 fixed points and it stops being a probabilistic check and becomes an identity, with no challenge and no hash. Cost is then roughly 7 x 89 = 623 certified F_p multiplications for a full 256-bit variable-base scalar multiplication, against a current 62-step GLV loop. THE ONE THING TO DERIVE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: what is the exact degree of the verification identity as a rational function of A0, counting numerator and denominator separately, and how many fixed evaluation points force it? If that number is small, this replaces the entire scalar-mul architecture. Also note the agent's corollary: if ECIP works, GLV and the lattice relation become redundant, since cost does not depend on scalar size. Source: Liam Eagen, eprint 2022/596; reference impl garaga hydra/garaga/hints/ecip.py.

SHARPENED by an independent study of Wesolowski/Pietrzak proofs of exponentiation, which found the same disease in a case where it could be made fully explicit: with a compile-time challenge the verification equation becomes a BIJECTION from the free witness onto the claimed output, so every output has an accepting proof and the gadget is vacuous. Apply exactly that test here before spending anything: at a single fixed A0, does the ECIP check remain surjective onto Q as the divisor witness coefficients range freely? If yes -- and with a_num/a_den/b_num/b_den all free I expect yes -- then single-point ECIP is vacuous, NOT merely unproven, and the deg+1-fixed-points derandomisation is the ONLY version worth deriving. See _meta.fixed_challenge_rule.

leads.summary: Eliminate lambda from affine addition: 3 certificates + a lambda witness -> 2 certificates and no lambda. (x3+x1+x2)(x1-x2)^2 = (y1-y2)^2 (deg 3) and (y3+y2)(x1-x2) = (y1-y2)(x1-x3) (deg 2). Doubling likewise 3 -> 2.
leads.note: gnark keeps lambda and does NOT do this, so it is not folklore. DIRECTLY COMPARABLE TO WHAT WE ALREADY PRICE: this is the II.14 degree ladder -- deleting a witness by raising a certificate's degree. Our own table says D=2 -> D=3 costs +240 and materialising a value costs 531, so the trade is only worth taking where the degree rise is affordable, and the table also says D=3 is INFEASIBLE at 4x64 (the folded position exceeds 2^253) and fine at 8x32. So this lead is COUPLED to fb-base32-fold and to which fold a site sits on -- price it per site, on the 32-bit sites first. Do not sweep.

leads.summary: Check whether limb convolutions are paying schoolbook k^2 rows where Winograd rank says 2k-1 suffice. Evaluation and interpolation are CONSTANT matrices, hence free, so a k-limb product needs only 2k-1 PRODUCT rows. At k=64 that is 127 rather than 4096.
leads.note: VERIFY BEFORE BELIEVING -- I have NOT confirmed our tree is schoolbook, and I think it probably is not. The claim came from reading a squaring's cost as <3925,4096> and observing 4096 = 64^2, but that cost includes range checks and carry certification, NOT just convolution products, so the coincidence may be exactly that. Our tree already has interpolatedMul and interpolatedMulX (an n1-vector by an n2-vector at n1+n2-1 points), which IS the 2k-1 form -- so the technique is likely already deployed and this lead is then worth zero. THE ONE CHECK: count the actual product rows inside ONE squaring in records/rsa-.../SquareModBalGT.lean and compare against 2k-1 for its limb count. If it is already 2k-1, close this. TWO GENUINELY NEW SUB-ITEMS THAT SURVIVE EITHER WAY: (a) cyclic convolution of length N has rank exactly N when N divides r-1, and BN254's r-1 has 2-adic valuation 28, so every power-of-two length up to 2^28 has a root of unity available -- an NTT with free constant transforms; soundness needs the true convolution cells below r, which at k=64,b=64 is 2b+log2(k) = 134 < 254, fine. (b) IF THE MODULUS IS A PUBLIC INPUT the q*n convolution is witness-times-constant, i.e. entirely free. Check whether n is public in this challenge -- that one is cheap to answer and potentially large. Same audit applies to secp256k1, where '2k-1-point multiply witnesses 15 cells' suggests 8-limb Toom is already in place.

leads.summary: A rank-r quadratic relation costs ceil(r/2) rows, not r. Homogenise P to a symmetric matrix, congruence-diagonalise (the resulting linear forms are FREE), then pair terms into hyperbolic planes: a*L^2 + b*M^2 = a*(L+cM)(L-cM) with c^2 = -b/a.
leads.note: GENERAL TECHNIQUE, NOT A SITE -- applies to every degree-2 certificate in every tree, which is most of them. The mechanism: diagonalising a quadratic form is a free change of basis because affine combinations cost nothing, and each hyperbolic pair collapses two squares into ONE product. If c^2 = -b/a is a non-residue, mix in a third index; Chevalley-Warning guarantees isotropy for r >= 3, so the pairing never gets stuck. Combined with 'never assert your last equation' (II.11) the emit is ceil(r/2) rows and ceil(r/2)-1 witnesses. FIRST MOVE: take one existing degree-2 certificate whose relation has visible rank above 2 -- the GroupedEq family is the obvious candidate -- compute the rank of its symmetric matrix, and see whether ceil(r/2) is below what it currently pays. NOT YET PRICED AT ANY SITE.

leads.summary: Deterministic permutation / multiset-equality certificate with NO random challenge: a Waksman network of 1-row switches. Cost 2(n log2 n - n + 1) score. n=64 -> 642, n=1024 -> 18434.
leads.note: THE SWITCH IS THE NEW PART AND IT IS WORTH KNOWING ON ITS OWN. The textbook selector out1 = a + s(b-a) with s boolean costs 2 rows + 2 witnesses. Instead witness ONLY out1 and assert (out1 - a)(out1 - b) = 0, then take out2 = a + b - out1 as a free affine. That pins {out1,out2} = {a,b} as a MULTISET in one row and one witness. Waksman's network realises every permutation in S_n with n log2 n - n + 1 such switches, so the constraint variety is exactly {(x, pi(x))} -- no challenge, no grand product, and therefore expressible as an unconditional Lean soundness theorem, which the grand-product argument is NOT. NOTHING IN THE CURRENT FIVE CHALLENGES NEEDS THIS. Recorded because it is the correct answer to sorting, RAM, and set-equality if one ever appears, and because the 1-row two-root switch is a I.4-family gadget (decoy roots) we did not have.

leads.summary: n-ary XOR of booleans: for n >= 7 extract the parity from the FREE sum instead of building an XOR3 tree. Witness the m = ceil(log2(floor(n/2)+1)) bits of q, assert (s-2q)(s-2q-1) = 0; parity is the free affine s-2q. Cost 2m+1 vs 2*ceil((n-1)/2).
leads.note: Crossover is at n=7 (tree 6 vs free-sum 5); it widens fast -- n=15 gives 14 vs 7, n=31 gives 30 vs 9, n=63 gives 62 vs 11. Linear becomes logarithmic. SOUNDNESS: q is a genuine integer in [0, 2^m - 1] via its own bits, and s - 2q in {0,1} forces q = floor(s/2) uniquely; a superset range is safe whenever 2q+1 > n is unreachable. NOT APPLICABLE TO KECCAK THETA -- its widest XOR is the 5-way column parity, which is below the crossover, and see keccak-theta-slp for why materialising anything wider loses. The general form is Paterson-Stockmeyer: any SYMMETRIC boolean function is a univariate in the free sum s, evaluable in about 2*sqrt(n) products (m non-scalar mults reach degree floor((m+2)^2/4)). Look for symmetric subfunctions before building trees. NEGATIVE WORTH KEEPING: generic bit-packing into base-8/base-13 digits of one field element never helps, because the unpacking identity was ALREADY free and packing forces you to witness digits that were free affine forms. That is distinct from I.2 lambda-packing, which is genuine but needs the packed output consumed additively.

leads.summary: Rewrite Sigma0/Sigma1/sigma0/sigma1 in carry-save form and never materialise them. A+B+C = (A xor B xor C) + 2*maj(A,B,C) over the integers, so each becomes a FREE integer affine combination of rotations minus twice a majority word.
leads.source: SHA-256 reformulation research, 2026-08-10, verified on 1e5 random inputs per function and on 1e5 full-round states
leads.note: COST-NEUTRAL BY ITSELF -- a maj bit and an xor3 bit are both <1,1>, and maj = (s - xor3)/2 with s free, so they are affinely interchangeable. ITS VALUE IS AS A PRECONDITION: it is what makes sha-sigma-trunc's free top bit exist, it enables sha-shr-pack, and it deletes four 32-bit intermediate words per round from the witness. The fused round becomes e' == d + h + K + W + [ROTR6+ROTR11+ROTR25](e) + Ch(e,f,g) - 2N1 (mod 2^32), and a' the same plus [ROTR2+ROTR13+ROTR22](a) + Maj(a,b,c) - 2N0. Sigma0, Sigma1, T1 and T2 are never materialised; the whole nonlinearity of a round is three majority words and one Ch word. FIRST STEP: prove in Lean that A + B + C = (A ^^^ B ^^^ C) + 2 * maj A B C over Nat restricted to < 2^32, then rewrite the round to emit N0, N1 and fold the rotation sums into the existing free linear combination.

leads.summary: The SHR positions of sigma0/sigma1 feed compile-time ZEROS, so their gadgets degenerate from degree 3 to degree 2 -- maj(A,B,0) = A AND B, xor3(A,B,0) = A XOR B -- and degree-2 gadgets pack TWO per row. sigma0 positions 29-30 and sigma1 positions 22-30.
leads.note: 5 rows per schedule step, 240 per block. THE UNDERLYING DICHOTOMY IS THE REUSABLE PART AND IT IS PROVED: a gadget's MULTILINEAR DEGREE over the boolean cube decides everything. Degree 2 (Ch, XOR2, AND2) takes the C-slot shape gamma*z = P0*Q0 - R0 and packs EXACTLY 2 per row -- never 3, because for k gadgets on disjoint variables the quadratic form is a direct sum of k rank->=1 blocks and the C-slot shape needs rank <= 2 modulo the free diagonal shifts. Degree 3 (Maj, XOR3, AND3) takes the non-vanishing-multiplier shape and packs NEVER -- proved, including against decoy roots, by applying the bi-non-affine projector: z^2 contributes 2*lambda*f~ (x) g~ which nothing else in the row can match. Exhaustive search over multipliers with coefficients in [-3,3] agrees: zero hits for MAJ+MAJ, XOR3+XOR3, XOR3+MAJ, MAJ+CH, AND3+MAJ, including pairs sharing one or two inputs. SO: stop looking for a row that packs two Maj or two XOR3. That search is closed. circomlib captures part of this (its O1 pass kills mid = b*c for 13 bits per SigmaPlus, 624 constraints) but neither the packing of the surviving degree-2 gadgets nor the free top bit appears in any implementation found.

leads.summary: The message-schedule quotient is exactly 2 bits. Machine-checked over 2e5 random 4-tuples: q_i in {0,1,2,3}, and it follows immediately because after the -2n corrections all four terms are genuine 32-bit words so their sum is < 4*2^32.
leads.note: CHECK WHAT WE CURRENTLY CHARGE BEFORE PRICING THIS -- if MessageSchedule.lean already witnesses 2 bits the item is worth zero; if it charges 3 bits or a product chain, replace with two witnessed bits and let the reduction row absorb q = q0 + 2*q1 for free. The whole schedule step is one free affine form plus two majority words plus this quotient: the bracketed rotation/shift sum plus W[i-7] plus W[i-16] is ENTIRELY FREE, and the only nonlinearity is -2*n1(W[i-2]) - 2*n0(W[i-15]). Carries cannot be shared across words -- each W feeds exactly one sigma0 and one sigma1 in its lifetime and the majority words of different steps have disjoint variable sets. NEGATIVE WORTH KEEPING: the SHA-2 cryptanalysis literature on the linearised schedule (Rijmen-Oswald, Pramstaller et al., Matusiewicz-Pieprzyk, Mendel et al.) does NOT hand us this decomposition -- it replaces + by XOR and studies the code's minimum weight, discarding the carry correction as the thing that makes linearisation approximate. That is the term we need.

leads.summary: CLOSED DIRECTIONS, recorded so they are not re-explored. Sparse/spread representation, meet-in-the-middle, alternative rotation-friendly representations, and rank/tensor diagonalisation of the Sigma words are all dead, each for a structural reason.
leads.note: (1) SPARSE/SPREAD (halo2 table16, 2099 rows) -- the ENTIRE saving is that the dense<->spread bijection is one LOOKUP row. Enforcing it arithmetically means decomposing the 16-bit chunk into bits and re-summing with weights 4^i, i.e. back to >=1 row per bit. No lookup-free variant exists or can. (2) MEET-IN-THE-MIDDLE -- the backward round invokes the IDENTICAL four nonlinear gadgets on the identical words; the bijection is realised entirely by free affine rearrangement, so direction does not touch the nonlinear content. Zero gain, and note the feed-forward is NOT what blocks it. (3) ROTATION-FRIENDLY REPRESENTATIONS (roots of unity in F_r, F_2[x]/(x^32-1)) -- every invertible linear change of representation is free in BOTH directions, so it cannot change the cost of anything. The bit vector already has rotation free AND addition free; the only cost is re-decomposition, which is intrinsic to the nonlinear interface. (4) RANK/TENSOR DIAGONALISATION of the Sigma words -- the quadratic part is rank <= 32 and would give 16 rows, but the cubic part T = sum 2^j x_{j+u} x_{j+v} x_{j+w} is a DIAGONAL 3-tensor with 32 nonzero entries, slice rank exactly 32, so >= ceil(32/3) = 11 multiplications for T alone and realistically 32. THE LESSON: the non-vanishing-multiplier row is extraordinarily good precisely because it computes a degree-3 function in ONE row by hiding the degree in a division. Rank methods must pay for degree 3 explicitly and cannot compete. (5) A GENUINE BUT SMALL ITEM, not a dead end: for the FIRST block the state is the constant IV, so round 0's gadgets are compile-time constants and at round 1 both Maj and Ch have two constant arguments and collapse to free affine functions. Worth about 2 rounds on block 1 only.
